description: The Global Terrorism Database is an event database of terrorist attacks worldwide, whose incident records include the nature of the target, so that attacks on infrastructure can be separated from other attacks. It covers events from 1970 to 2020, with more than 200,000 cases, and grew from data first collected by the Pinkerton Global Intelligence Services (PGIS) and acquired in 2001. It is maintained by START at the University of Maryland. The data are available for download after completing a contact-information form, under an end user licence agreement that grants a non-commercial research licence and forbids redistribution; they are free for that use. Caveats: the release described ends in 2020, and the licence rules out commercial use and sharing of the data. It supports threat characterisation and physical attack scenarios for critical infrastructure risk studies; a related record is the multi-domain incidents dataset for critical infrastructure.
